metadata.title: ECIS — Episode 3: Three Models, Zero Shortcuts
metadata.color_semantics: Claude fidelity UI beats (B00 ask, B07 verdict, B08 handoff, B09 outro) stay cream/ink/terracotta per CLAUDE-BRAND.md. Body beats (B01-B06) illustrate the three-model pipeline mechanism itself — dark stage (#0a0a0f), same PEDAGOGY-approved deviation as Episodes 1 and 2. Purple (Llama) and teal (Mistral) carry over unchanged from Episode 2; amber (#D9A757, Qwen) is this episode's new series color, to be kept consistent in any future episode that reuses this model.
metadata.greeting_note: Plain English hello, narrator is Anjana; no channel handle or brand chip on this build.
metadata.note: Fresh build — derived from examples/ecis-ep3/script.md + visuals/*.md (original pre-production briefs). Beats B00 (ask), B07 (verdict), B08 (your-turn handoff), B09 (title outro) added per the ai-explainer shared skeleton and the your-turn closing standard; the six body beats (B01-B06) come from script.md's six narration beats, kept verbatim (already tight, no trim needed). Source voice was listed as am_onyx in README.md/script.md/beats.json — overridden to af_bella (Anjana, no handle) per the series convention established in Episodes 1 and 2. The B06 close beat's original narration/visual claimed a twenty-five-company run this episode did not perform (implementation-only week) — corrected to 'every input gated' before this beat sheet was authored (see PEDAGOGY.md Scope correction). GATE P signed (see PEDAGOGY.md — VERDICT: PASS); audio, clips, and final render are complete. Two visual QC fixes made after the first compile: B03's three rejected-chunk labels were converging to the same on-screen position and overlapping into unreadable text (fixed by giving each chunk its own drop target), and B04's four provenance layers were almost entirely hidden behind the signal card (fixed by staggering them into a visible cascading stack below the card). Both re-rendered and re-verified against fresh frame grabs before the final compile.

beats.narration_text: Last episode, ECIS ran two models side by side across twenty-five companies. I'm Anjana — here's what changed this week: a third model, and the discipline to keep it honest.

show.event: ClaudeComposerAsk: greeting 'Hello, Anjana'; ask types itself
runningText 'loading this week's build…'
output lines resolve: 'a third model, native not bolted on' / 'quality gates on input and output' / 'full provenance on every signal'

props.command: Last time, ECIS ran two LLMs voting side by side. This week you added a third model and reworked the pipeline for quality control and full provenance. Can you show me what changed?
output: a third model, native not bolted on
quality gates on input and output

beats.narration_text: Last time, ECIS had two models reading every earnings call. Llama and Mistral, side by side. That was episode two. Now there are three.

show.event: the dual-model architecture from Episode 2 appears instantly, fully formed — Llama and Mistral feeding the triangulator
hold — recognizable callback to Episode 2
the frame pulls back slightly; a dotted-outline slot fades in on the right, teasing what's coming

beats.narration_text: Qwen two point five, fourteen billion parameters. Twice the size of the other two. It runs the same pipeline, the same prompts, the same self-consistency checks. But it sees things differently. More reliable on structured output. Fewer retries on the responses. The architecture was reworked so multi-model is not an add-on anymore. Model identity flows through the pipeline state. The triangulator weighs all three independently.

show.event: a third node animates in to the right of Llama and Mistral — 'Qwen 14B' in amber, visibly larger, reflecting the parameter count
a pipeline-state bar appears below the nodes with three colored dots; label: 'Model identity flows through state.'
the triangulator opens to show three independent weight bars, one per model
a chunk flows through all three: Llama 'raised 0.81', Mistral 'raised 0.77', Qwen 'raised 0.84' — triangulator outputs 'raised 0.86', boosted by three-way agreement
label lands: 'Multi-model native. Not bolted on.'

beats.narration_text: More models means more signals. More signals means more noise if you are not careful. So the pipeline now gates its own input. Chunks that are empty, mostly boilerplate, or too short are rejected before any reader sees them. And on the output side, signals below a minimum confidence threshold are logged for audit but excluded from the scorecard. The system tracks what it is uncertain about without letting that uncertainty pollute its accuracy metrics.

show.event: INPUT GATE — a conveyor belt; a gate barrier appears before the readers
three chunks are stopped and stamped: EMPTY, BOILERPLATE 0.87, TOO SHORT; they drop into a 'Rejection Log' bin below
good chunks continue through unimpeded
OUTPUT GATE — a second gate appears after the triangulator
one signal at confidence 0.31 hits the gate, gets tagged LOW CONFIDENCE, and diverts into an 'Audit Log' bin
label lands: 'Logged. Not scored.'

beats.narration_text: Every signal ECIS produces now stores the exact prompt that created it. The system prompt, the few-shot examples it retrieved, the temporal context from prior quarters, and the chunk itself. If a signal looks wrong six months from now, you can rebuild the exact conditions that produced it and re-run the extraction. Same model, same prompt, same answer. Nothing is a black box. Every decision has a receipt.

show.event: a signal card appears center screen — ticker, direction, confidence, supporting quote
four layers fan out behind the card: System Prompt, Few-Shot Examples (3), Temporal Context, Source Chunk
label lands: 'Full provenance. Fully reproducible.'
a receipt icon stamps onto the card — a visual seal

beats.narration_text: The dashboard now shows all three models in one view. Calibration curves overlaid on the same chart. Brier scores side by side. Signal counts per model. You can filter by ticker, by model, by confidence range, and drill into any signal to see its full provenance. One screen to see how three models read the same market.

show.event: calibration curve panel — three lines (purple Llama, teal Mistral, amber Qwen) draw against the diagonal
Brier score comparison — three grouped bars per metric
signal explorer table gains a Model column; a filter dropdown selects 'Qwen 14B'
one row is tapped, expanding to show the provenance stack from B04

beats.narration_text: Three models. Every input gated. Every signal traceable. ECIS, episode three.

show.event: flash 1: triple-node architecture (purple, teal, amber) — on 'three models'
flash 2: the conveyor-belt quality-gate visual from B03 — on 'every input gated'
flash 3: the provenance stack from B04 — on 'every signal traceable'
title lands center screen: 'ECIS — Episode 3'

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. A third model joined the pipeline, and multi-model support is now native to its architecture. The pipeline gates its own input and output, logging what it's uncertain about instead of scoring it. Every signal now stores its own provenance — the exact prompt, examples, and context that produced it. And the dashboard shows all three models' calibration, side by side.

show.event: 0.5s lead pause, then ClaudeVerdictArtifact card builds in
line 1: triple-node icon settles in
line 2: gate-barrier icon settles in
line 3: provenance-stack icon settles in

artifactLines: A third model, Qwen 14B, joined natively — not bolted on.
Input and output quality gates keep noise out of the scorecard.
Every signal now carries full, reproducible provenance.
The dashboard shows all three models side by side.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. "I have a process at work that produces outputs I trust without ever checking why it's uncertain, or being able to reproduce exactly how a specific output was generated. Can you help me: one, design a way to log every low-confidence output separately instead of silently averaging it into my results; two, define what 'full provenance' would even mean for my process — what would I need to store to rebuild any specific output later; and three, tell me honestly whether the record-keeping overhead is worth it for how often I'd actually need to look back?" Paste that into Claude and see whether your own pipeline has a black box hiding in it.

show.event: ClaudeComposerAsk: greeting 'Your turn.'; prompt types itself into the composer
runningText 'checking for a hidden black box…'
